prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1122; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured's policyholder reporting a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. The claimant was driving the vehicle at the time and reports a back strain shortly afterward.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force when the loss occurred. No issues found with the policy status.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. Witness statements and scene photographs are consistent with the accident happening as described by all parties.

Entry 4: Reviewed the damage photos and repair estimate. The front-end damage matches the described impact, and nothing in the file suggests earlier damage to the vehicle.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant, who is not represented, about the injury. The account given matches what was reported at first notice. The back strain is a plausible injury for a collision of this type.

Entry 6: Medical records show a course of treatment that followed a usual pattern and tapered off as the claimant improved. The claimant mentioned a minor strain in the same area years ago that healed fully, and that prior history has been noted in the file.

Entry 7: Follow-up call with the claimant confirmed the same account of events as in every prior conversation. Based on the records and corroborating evidence, the bodily injury portion of the claim is proceeding through standard review.
